key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: GRADUAL, CHRONIC/RECURRENT over weeks to months (not acute). Often after meals or when lying down. LOCATION: RETROSTERNAL (behind breastbone) and EPIGASTRIC. BURNING rises from stomach toward throat. No radiation to arms/jaw. DURATION: Episodes last minutes to hours. Can be constant if severe reflux. May persist after meals. CHARACTER: BURNING sensation (heartburn). NOT sharp or pressure-like (would suggest cardiac). Acid rising sensation. AGGRAVATING: WORSE AFTER MEALS, when LYING DOWN, or BENDING OVER. Spicy foods, caffeine, alcohol, large meals trigger. RELIEVING: ANTACIDS provide quick relief. SITTING UPRIGHT helps. Elevation of head during sleep helps. TIMING: EPISODIC - worse after meals, at night when lying flat. Pattern repeats with dietary triggers. SEVERITY: 3-6/10, mild to moderate discomfort. Not severe. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: SOUR TASTE (acid regurgitation), belching, dysphagia (if chronic), chronic cough, hoarseness. KEY POSITIVES: Antacid relief, worse when lying down, chronic pattern, dietary triggers. KEY NEGATIVES: NEW SEVERE chest pain requires cardiac workup FIRST. Dysphagia with weight loss suggests stricture/cancer. Hematemesis suggests ulcer.

includes.patient_friendly: upper middle part of your belly

red_flags: New severe chest pain - rule out cardiac causes (myocardial infarction (MI), angina) FIRST before attributing to gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD)
Dysphagia (difficulty swallowing) with weight loss - esophageal stricture or cancer, needs endoscopy
Vomiting blood or black tarry stools - GI bleeding from severe esophagitis or ulcer
Symptoms not responding to PPI therapy - consider alternative diagnosis or Barrett's esophagus
